Discussion: Presented by Yunlu Wu (ZTE). This contribution provides the initial consideration on the potential mobility related issue caused by the large number of vehicles with high speed in V2X. Following observations and proposals are made: Observation 1: The HOF increases significantly when UE moves in high speed. Observation 2: For all scenarios except for the one to many sidelink communication configured with UE autonomous resource allocation configuration, high HOF would result in severe service interruption and extra delay of V2X message delivery. Observation 3: For all scenarios, the S1/X2 signalling load increase significantly due to frequent HOs and TAU(s) for the large number of vehicles with high speed in V2X. Therefore it is proposed to make an initial agreement on the issues for a large number of vehicles in high mobility. An LS should be sent to RAN2/RAN1 for their evaluation. Chairman: Does not agree that high speed or large number of mobiles bring specific problems to mobility. Decision: Noted Discussion: Decision: Not Treated *************************************************** -> Offline (LGE): - Way Forward - For PC5 interface: RAN3 should discuss authorization aspects and resource coordination only - For Uu based coordination: - Multiple Operators Support is enabled by inter-PLMN coordination. - RAN3 did not se any restrictions related to existing network sharing deployment scenarios in the context of V2V, - TP might be considered for the TR - V2x should support inter-PLMN coordination - Network sharing may be seen as a solution, but it is costly for operators - In R3-160505 Discussion: Presented by Jian Xu (LGE). Steven Xu (Nokia Networks): In 5.2: "is non neglible" -> WF is endorsed unseen in R3-150567. Decision: Noted Discussion: Presented by Jian Xu (LGE). R3-160529 includes the TPs from the following tdocs: - R3-160519 - R3-160540 - R3-160541 - editorials -> The TP is agreed unseen in R3-160568. Decision: Noted

This contribution provides the initial consideration on the potential mobility related issue caused by the large number of vehicles with high speed in V2X. Following observations and proposals are made: Observation 1: The HOF increases significantly when UE moves in high speed. Observation 2: For all scenarios except for the one to many sidelink communication configured with UE autonomous resource allocation configuration, high HOF would result in severe service interruption and extra delay of V2X message delivery. Observation 3: For all scenarios, the S1/X2 signalling load increase significantly due to frequent HOs and TAU(s) for the large number of vehicles with high speed in V2X. Therefore it is proposed to make an initial agreement on the issues for a large number of vehicles in high mobility. An LS should be sent to RAN2/RAN1 for their evaluation. Chairman: Does not agree that high speed or large number of mobiles bring specific problems to mobility. Decision: Noted Discussion: Decision: Not Treated *************************************************** -> Offline (LGE): - Way Forward - For PC5 interface: RAN3 should discuss authorization aspects and resource coordination only - For Uu based coordination: - Multiple Operators Support is enabled by inter-PLMN coordination. - RAN3 did not se any restrictions related to existing network sharing deployment scenarios in the context of V2V, - TP might be considered for the TR - V2x should support inter-PLMN coordination - Network sharing may be seen as a solution, but it is costly for operators - In R3-160505 Discussion: Presented by Jian Xu (LGE). Steven Xu (Nokia Networks): In 5.2: "is non neglible" -> WF is endorsed unseen in R3-150567. Decision: Noted Discussion: Presented by Jian Xu (LGE). R3-160529 includes the TPs from the following tdocs: - R3-160519 - R3-160540 - R3-160541 - editorials -> The TP is agreed unseen in R3-160568. Decision: Noted
